wellbeing_quotes.quote: Ready for the blackout CSV import or the overlap report whenever you are - though both are admin-screen wiring, which is more surface area than I'd want to hand you at this hour if it can wait.

winddown_quotes.quote: Two notes for when you're rested, neither blocking:
Everything's verified, nothing's half-done - a good place to stop.
The two predicates are named and so the asymmetry is visible rather than accidental - but it is an asymmetry, worth a look when you're fresh.
One decision you should sanity-check when you're rested.** An unreadable - , or - is treated as *no window*, exactly like the importer's absent .
Ready for the blackout CSV import or the overlap report whenever you are - though both are admin-screen wiring, which is more surface area than I'd want to hand you at this hour if it can wait.

subtasks.name: s1 an inverted range is rejected and a forward range still passes
s2 a stay over the 30 night cap is rejected and exactly 30 is allowed
s3 a same day range is valid with zero nights
s4 every rejection carries a machine readable code beside its reason
s5 a date that is not a real calendar day is rejected as bad_format
s6 a quote carries the rejection code and a day-use stay prices from its own rate
s7 a per-property night cap overrides the default and the reason names the cap that applied
s8 a blackout date inside the occupied nights rejects, and the check-out day is not one
s9 totals are rounded to whole cents and an unusable nightly rate is refused
s10 overlaps tells a genuine clash from a turnover
s11 the booking window applies only with a today, and the rejection order is fixed
s12 nightsByMonth splits the occupied nights across calendar months
